results.name: recency_out_of_range_yes
results.description: Yes rate for targets outside the examples' [min,max] span (sets of 2+ examples) that lie strictly closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown one; observed above null means people generalize more around the most recent example than the order-blind model predicts (recency).
results.code:
# name: recency_out_of_range_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets outside the examples' [min,max] span (sets of 2+ examples) that lie strictly closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown one; observed above null means people generalize more around the most recent example than the order-blind model predicts (recency).
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    first = X[:, 0]
    last = X[np.arange(len(X)), n - 1]
    m = (n >= 2) & ((t < mn) | (t > mx)) & (np.abs(t - last) < np.abs(t - first))
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0

results.name: single_shared_final_digit_yes
results.description: Yes rate for targets whose final digit matches exactly one example's final digit (sets of 2+ examples, target not itself an example); observed below null means the model over-weights a single shared last digit (ends-in rules) relative to people.
results.code:
# name: single_shared_final_digit_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets whose final digit matches exactly one example's final digit (sets of 2+ examples, target not itself an example); observed below null means the model over-weights a single shared last digit (ends-in rules) relative to people.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    fd = np.nansum((X % 10) == (t % 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & (fd == 1) & (dist > 0)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0

results.name: within_cell_disagreement
results.description: Mean over (set, target) cells with 2+ responses of the unbiased within-cell variance k(m-k)/(m(m-1)) of the yes responses; observed above null means respondents disagree with each other on the same item more than one shared posterior predicts (individual differences the model lacks), below null means they agree more.
results.code:
# name: within_cell_disagreement
# description: Mean over (set, target) cells with 2+ responses of the unbiased within-cell variance k(m-k)/(m(m-1)) of the yes responses; observed above null means respondents disagree with each other on the same item more than one shared posterior predicts (individual differences the model lacks), below null means they agree more.
def test_statistic(df):
    g = df.assign(_y=df["rating"].astype(float)).groupby(["number_set", "target"])["_y"].agg(["sum", "size"])
    g = g[g["size"] >= 2]
    k = g["sum"].to_numpy()
    m = g["size"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    return float(np.mean(k * (m - k) / (m * (m - 1)))) if len(g) else 0.0
